To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology of ZnO nanostructures immobilized on honeycomb support has a significant effect on the sorption performance for H 2 S and/or COS removal from syngas.
the morphology of nanostructured ZnS-loaded ceramic honeycombs significantly influences the performance of the sorbents in syngas desulphurization.

Nanostructured ZnO with high surface area, crystallinity, and surface coverage was successfully immobilized on honeycomb substrate through a facile seeding-growth method and showed significantly higher sorption capacity than commercial ZnO sorbens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of nanostructured ZnS-loaded honeycomb for synga desulfurization, where the morphology of ZnO nanomaterials is found to have a significant impact on the sorption performance.
the synthesis of nanostructured ZnS-loaded ceramic honeycomb and its application as a novel sorbent for removal of sulfur species from syngas.
the preparation and application of nanostructured ZnS-loaded honeycomb for synga desulfurization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the morphology of ZnO has a strong influence on the sorption capacity of syngas desulphurization.

the nanostructured ZnO loaded on the honeycomb support with nanosheet morphology (ZnO-ns) showed significantly better sulfur sorption performance than the ZnO with nanodot, nanorod and commercial morphology.
the ZnO-nanostructured sorbent has the potential to be used for syngas cleaning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nanostructured ZnO-nS loaded ceramic honeycomb showed better performance in syngas desulphurization due to its higher crystallinity, surface coverage, and higher density of the reactive sites compared to the commercial sorbents.
ZnO sorbents with nanosheet morphology and high surface area have better performance in syngas desulphurization than the commercial ZnO sorbet.
nanostructured ZnO sorbents with different morphologies were synthesized and immobilized on a ceramic honeycomb support.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of ZnO plays a critical role in its performance as a sorbent for syngas cleanup.
the surface morphology of ZnO sorbents has a significant effect on their performance for syngas sulfur removal.
the nanostructured morphology of ZnO can have significant influence on the sorption performance of the immobilized ZnO sorbents for syngas purification.
